parsedVerdict.reasoning: Subscription.ts is a domain entity, and most of it does domain work: the seat-limit invariants in start/resize and the state transitions in cancel. The problem is the field `private readonly repo = new InMemorySubscriptionRepository();`. The entity builds this persistence object itself, and the class comes from src/infrastructure/persistence, a layer the domain may not depend on. The rubric treats persistence done through a class of a layer the model doesn't allow as direct I/O in a domain file, and here the entity creates that class rather than having it injected. That makes persistence a responsibility of the entity, which belongs to the infrastructure layer. The field is never used, but the rubric judges what a declaration is, not only what it does at run time, so it still fails. The import-direction breach itself is out of scope here. What fails this rule is the misplaced persistence role. No candidate flags were raised.

violations.message: The domain entity Subscription creates and holds an infrastructure persistence object (`private readonly repo = new InMemorySubscriptionRepository()`, from src/infrastructure/persistence). Persistence is an infrastructure-layer job. The domain can't depend on that layer, and an entity shouldn't set up its own repository.
